rows.why: He said lazim alone for 'I had to'; Amal recast with kaan laazem.
rows.english: I had to teach her everything
rows.r3_challenge: Amal said at 05:04 'It works I should have, and it works as I had to teach her' - she accepted his laazem (should have) as valid, so La-lazim -> كان لازم is not a correction; 'La-' may also be the engine's rendering of kaan.

rows.chat: EL-YOAM Benet 3ammi badat/ballashat teshte8el fi ma7alli u kaan laazem a3allemha kulshi
rows.why: ta3allamt-ha is 'I learned' (get side, past); to teach her is the doubled-middle a3allemha, bare present after kaan laazem - Amal recast.

rows.medi_said: make her a good [speaking Arabic] Would it be [speaking Arabic] ?
rows.amal_said: Let her be. ... أخليها تصير ... أنا لازم تصير؟ No. You'd need something like to make her، to make to let her become.
rows.chat: bas ana ra7 ajrreb a5alliha t9eer muwazzafe mnee7a
rows.why: Amal echoed his form 'أنا لازم تصير؟' and said No, then gave a5alliha t9eer; low because he offered it as 'would it be ...?' and his Arabic is hidden by the engine.
rows.english: I'll try to make her become a good employee
rows.proposed_rule: To make / let someone become X use a5alli + object ending + bare verb (a5alliha t9eer), not laazem + verb.

rows.why: English calque 'one more' with أكتر; Amal recast كمان واحد, and recast it again at 10:19 when he repeated واحد أكتر at 10:17 (one row, the first).

rows.amal_said: Made. ... Past. He made me excited.
rows.why: He used the present for 'he made me excited'; Amal prompted 'Made... Past' and he fixed it to hamasni.

He added the present te- prefix to the command; Amal: just one T.

rows.why: For 'why aren't you excited (now)' he used a negated verb; Amal said use the adjective mit7ammse with mish.
'We got excited' needs the t- form t7ammasna (her chat); he said 7ammasna (we excited someone) and she let it pass on voice.
rows.r3_challenge: 'Uh, etna / hamasna' (19:14-19:19) may be e7na t-hamasna split by the engine (the t of t7ammasna in 'etna'); Amal said Mm-hmm. Needs audio.

rows.amal_said: الـ safar. Safra is one trip. Safar is...
rows.why: safra = one trip; for 'traveling' Amal recast el-safar.
'Excite me' needs the -ni object ending; Amal prompted 'Me' and he said hamasini.

rows.amal_said: Let's put it at the after.

kaan must take the I-ending: kunt ashte8el; Amal recast قُنت.
Working 'on' AI is fi in her chat; he said bi and she let it pass on voice.

rows.why: Object 'you (f)' after a vowel-final verb is -ki; Amal recast afarjiki.

rows.amal_said: We, we need to learn this verb نكمل. Continue.
rows.why: New verb kammel (continue) taught by Amal; he had not attempted it.
رجل is feminine so the verb takes t-; Amal said 'is feminine' and he fixed to بتوجع at 32:45.
After أنا the verb needs the I-form ba-wajj3ek (her chat); he used the he-form bey- twice and Amal moved on without voicing a fix.

rows.amal_said: is did I hurt you? Did you get hurt?
rows.why: He put an object ending on the get-hurt verb, which Amal said means 'did I hurt you'; he fixed to twajja3ti.

rows.amal_said: No, by me. ... Because of me.
rows.why: The get-hurt verb twajja3 takes min for 'by whom' (Amal 36:01: 'if you want to say by someone, then you'd use it'); he put -ni on the verb, she said No, by me, and he reached تواجهتي مني at 36:53. D2 = the verb's preposition, D3 = the ending on min.
rows.english: did you get hurt by me?

rows.why: For 'don't hurt her' he used the get-hurt t- verb with an object; Amal repeated the prompt, he moved to wajj3iha.
Negative command needs ma + the you-form (t-); Amal 'Very close', he fixed to ma tiwajaiha.
7aka takes la- for the listener (7akaiti-li, her chat); he put -ni straight on the verb and Amal said ممتاز, so it passed. Low: engine Latin.
rows.english: I got hurt by what you said to me
